brief: Goldman Sachs TMT specialist Sean Johnstone previews next week's Communacopia and Technology Conference in San Francisco, with over 260 companies and over 2,000 investors, all conference stats up on last year. Most-requested names in order: Datadog, CoreWeave, Microsoft, Shopify, Broadcom, AMD, Nvidia, Nebius, TSMC, Snowflake. The note poses three questions rather than making a house call. First, whether record spend on chips, power, data centres and networking is converting into visible software, cloud and application-layer revenue. The stated risk is that Nvidia's profits rest on investor capital flowing through model labs rather than self-sustaining customer economics further down the stack. Q2 evidence cited as constructive includes Palantir's 149% US commercial revenue growth, Snowflake's faster AI-enabled migrations, and monetisation gains at Tencent and Meta. Second, whether AI agents extend software value or pressure seat-based licensing. Third, capital discipline, where CoreWeave recontracting a 2020-vintage A100 SKU into 2029 and Google running seven-to-eight-year-old TPUs at 100% utilisation are offered as evidence older fleets retain value. Sector playbooks and the European names ASML, Adyen, SAP, Wise and Scout list debates to watch, not recommendations.
